sections.h2: What does Michigan charge in transfer tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Two separate levies apply to a deed given for money. The state levy is $3.75 on every $500 of value, rounded up for any leftover amount (MCL 207.525(1)). The county levy is 55 cents on the same $500 step in a county under 2,000,000 residents, and a county at or above that size may authorize up to 75 cents (MCL 207.504).

Stacked together, an ordinary Michigan county collects $8.60 for every $1,000 of price. Rounding works against the seller at the edges: a price of $200,000.01 lands in the next $500 bracket, which is why county charts list every bracket in turn.

The tax is collected when a deed or sales contract for consideration is recorded. The paper must show the total real property value on its face, or an affidavit with that value must ride along. In a sale that mixes land with furniture or equipment, only the real property is taxed, and only if the two values are stated separately.

sections.h2: What is the seller's bill at common sale prices?
sections.html:
A $250,000 sale in a county charging the standard 55 cents costs the seller $2,150 in combined tax. The table runs the statutory rates against round prices. Midland County's published chart and Monroe County's fee page agree with these figures.

Combined Michigan transfer tax by sale price, using the state and standard county rates
Sale priceState taxCounty taxTotal
$100,000$750$110$860
$150,000$1,125$165$1,290
$200,000$1,500$220$1,720
$250,000$1,875$275$2,150
$300,000$2,250$330$2,580

Midland County's chart shows $860 for any price in the bracket ending at $100,000, which matches the first row. Monroe County states the same rates as $7.50 and $1.10 per $1,000.

sections.h2: Who ends up paying at the closing table?
sections.html:
The statute puts liability for the state tax on the seller, or grantor. MCL 207.523(2) says so in one line, and subsection (3) sets the payment window: 15 days from delivery of the deed, paid to the treasurer of the county where the land lies. A title agent normally deducts the amount from sale proceeds and remits it as part of recording.

Nothing stops a purchase agreement from shifting the cost to the buyer. A buyer who pays on the seller's behalf can also ask for a refund if an exemption applied. Check the closing cost clause of your contract and request an itemized settlement statement before signing. A seller who later decides the sale qualified for an exemption can apply to the Department of Treasury under MCL 207.523(4).

sections.h2: Which sales escape the state tax?
sections.html:
Section 6 of the state act, MCL 207.526, runs through nearly two dozen exemptions. These come up most for homeowners:

  • A deed backed by less than $100 of consideration.
  • A gift deed from a parent to a son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child, or on to a grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • A corrective deed, including a quitclaim, that only confirms title the grantee already holds.
  • A transfer made through foreclosure or by deed in lieu, though the lender's later resale is taxed.
  • A court order or judgment that names no price.
  • A land contract under which legal title stays with the seller until the price is fully paid.
  • A deed that creates a joint tenancy when one of the joint owners already holds the property.

Leases, security instruments, and spousal deeds that make or end a tenancy by the entireties also fall outside the tax.

sections.h2: Does the county tax follow the same list?
sections.html:
Its list is shorter. MCL 207.505 exempts papers under $100, leases, security instruments, interests taxed as personal property, court judgments without a stated price, boundary line fixes, title confirmations, qualifying land contracts, mineral rights and certain joint tenancies. It has no entry for a gift to a child or grandchild, and it lacks the broad foreclosure exemption the state act contains.

That difference deserves a call before a parent deeds a house to a son or daughter for nominal money. Ask the county's recording office how it treats the particular deed.

sections.h2: Does the deed have to show the price?
sections.html:
Not necessarily. MCL 207.525(2) lets the parties attach an affidavit stating the total value in place of printing a price on the deed, and Treasury prescribes the form. Midland County's recording page makes the same point: a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit permits the price to be omitted.

Either route still produces a figure for the tax computation, and that figure later reaches the assessor through the buyer's transfer affidavit. Keep the deed, the affidavit and the settlement statement consistent.

sections.h2: Is a land contract sale taxed differently?
sections.html:
While legal title remains with the seller, a land contract is exempt from both layers of transfer tax. For property tax purposes it still counts as a transfer of ownership under MCL 211.27a(6)(b): taxable value resets for the calendar year after signing and does not reset a second time when the deed finally records.

A seller carrying a contract with a warranty clause should ask the treasurer's office about a tax certificate, since that kind of instrument cannot record without one.

sections.h2: What fees apply when the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30 per document under MCL 600.2567, however many pages it has. Five of those dollars feed the automation fund, and the remonumentation charge is built in. Assigning or discharging more than one instrument adds $3 for each extra, copies are $1 a page, and certification is $5. A charter county may set its own schedule by ordinance, so verify the amount locally.

After closing, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor a transfer notice under MCL 211.27a(10), and the new owner's taxable value resets the following year.

faqs.q: What is the state portion of Michigan's real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state portion is $3.75 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 under MCL 207.525(1), equal to $7.50 per $1,000.

faqs.q: What does the county add on top of that?
faqs.a: Fifty-five cents per $500, or $1.10 per $1,000, in a county with under 2,000,000 residents. A county of 2,000,000 or more may authorize up to 75 cents under MCL 207.504.

faqs.q: Will a deed from a parent to a child avoid the tax?
faqs.a: The state tax exempts a conveyance from an individual to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild under MCL 207.526(j) and (k). The county act has no matching entry, so ask the county recording office before relying on it.

faqs.q: Does a foreclosure deed carry transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state act exempts a deed given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. A later resale by the foreclosing entity is taxed. Confirm the county side with the local recording office.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost statewide?
faqs.a: The statutory fee is $30 per document, whatever the page count, under MCL 600.2567. A charter county can adopt a different schedule, and extra instrument references cost $3 each.
